extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal discipline proceedings; OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO Final Order implementing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the Office under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state-court discipline; describes procedural requirements, grounds, and post-exclusion obligations. Useful for practitioners facing reciprocal discipline and for Office staff implementing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion was ordered for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by causing his name to be removed from the roll of attorneys licensed to practice in Georgia by the Supreme Court of Georgia, a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order recites the state-court default findings (e.g., accepting client funds to file patent applications, representing they were filed when client could not confirm, failing to communicate, withdrawing without protecting client's interests or returning unearned fees, failing to provide proof or respond to investigation) as the factual basis for reciprocal discipline taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and response procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was mailed informing Respondent of the Complaint and that exclusion was requested; Respondent was directed that if he sought to contest imposition of exclusion he must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information he believes sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice was mailed by first-class certified mail, return-receipt requested, to the address on file; the mailing was returned undeliverable. If mail is undeliverable, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b) may be used. Failure to file a timely response supports a determination of no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for imposing reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not establish a genuine issue of material fact pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), exclusion identical to the discipline imposed by the state is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent bears the burden to produce all information sufficient to show a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based on the limited grounds set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). On default (no adequate response), the Office may determine there is no genuine issue and impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when mail undeliverable
rubrics_metrics.description: When mailed Notice and Order was returned as not deliverable and unable to be forwarded, the Office effected service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b) by publishing notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Official Gazette notifies the respondent that he may obtain a copy of the Notice and Order by sending a written request to the USPTO General Counsel. Publication is an alternative means of service where direct mail service fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order grants only a short limited recognition period (30 days) to facilitate compliance with 11.58(b) and otherwise requires full compliance with the obligations imposed by § 11.58 (responsibilities to clients, protection of client interests, return of client property/unearned fees) during exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with client-protection obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrowly-tailored, time-limited recognition allows the excluded practitioner to take actions necessary to protect clients and conclude pending matters consistent with § 11.58(b) only during the specified period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO, and shall not obtain any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and shall publish the specified NOTICE OF EXCLUSION in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner's exclusion and the basis for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice includes practitioner name, registration number, the regulatory violation cited (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)), and a summary of the state-court factual findings supporting the exclusion. Disciplinary decisions are also posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures reciprocal discipline and public awareness by notifying relevant state agencies and courts of the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition or request for reinstatement must meet the requirements set forth in § 11.60; the Final Order conditions restoration of privilege to practice on satisfying those regulatory reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and effect of published factual findings supporting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice summarizes the state court findings that provided the basis for discipline (e.g., client paid funds to file patent applications and for other legal work; practitioner said applications had been filed though client could not confirm; practitioner became unavailable; practitioner withdrew without protecting client's interests or returning unearned fees; practitioner failed to provide proof or respond to investigation and notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual findings, when established by the state authority (even by default), form the factual predicate for reciprocal exclusion by the USPTO and will be publicly posted; such findings demonstrate the types of conduct (failure to communicate, failure to protect client interests, failure to account for/return fees, noncooperation with disciplinary authorities) that support exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory and regulatory bases empowering the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline based on state-bar actions; useful for understanding jurisdictional and procedural authority.
